frameworks.name: Wallet Objection Handling Framework
frameworks.definition: A structured five-step process to address wallet/payment objections during closing by confirming payment method availability upfront and providing alternative payment paths (ACH, Apple Wallet, delayed payment).

claims.text: Prospects who claim they left their wallet at home have not actually forgotten payment capability — they are signaling a deeper sales objection or hesitation about the commitment, because realistically no one leaves home without a payment method.
claims.speaker: Dr. Mosey
claims.mechanism: The claim serves as a diagnostic tool: when a prospect raises wallet objections, the root issue is usually unaddressed sales resistance, not actual payment unavailability.

claims.text: Requesting ID before requesting a payment card is mechanically easier and builds more trust, because the prospect expects to produce ID for verification whereas requesting a card directly can feel invasive; once the ID is shown and returned, the wallet is already exposed with payment methods visible.
claims.speaker: Dr. Mosey
conditions: At point of sale when payment is required
claims.mechanism: ID request creates a low-friction entry point to the wallet without directly asking for sensitive payment information; prospect seeing you return their ID builds permission for the next step (requesting payment method).

claims.text: When a prospect hesitates on payment method, use the banking app ACH approach as the primary backup path, because virtually 100% of people who bank have the banking app installed and can display their account number from statements in under 30 seconds.
claims.speaker: Dr. Mosey
conditions: When credit card is unavailable or prospect cannot access desired card
Requires merchant ACH payment processing capability
claims.mechanism: ACH transaction removes the need to carry a physical card and taps existing payment infrastructure the prospect already uses for banking, lowering friction.

numbers.axis: adoption rate of banking apps among banked populations

bounded_by: Only applies to in-person and Zoom sales where phone access is available
Requires merchant to have ACH processing enabled

claims.text: Apple Wallet is a secondary fallback option for payment method substitution, but banking app ACH should be attempted first because banking app adoption and statement accessibility is higher than Apple Wallet adoption.
claims.speaker: Dr. Mosey
conditions: When credit card is unavailable and ACH approach failed
claims.mechanism: ACH has near-universal access (banking app), while Apple Wallet has lower adoption and requires specific device/ecosystem compatibility.

claims.text: When a prospect lacks immediate payment method availability, delaying payment 24 hours with a contract signed, combined with a mutual phone alarm reminder at the deposit time, closes the deal because it reframes the transaction as "lock in now, adjust payment method later" rather than rejecting the prospect's commitment.
claims.speaker: Dr. Mosey
conditions: Prospect has shown intent to buy but cannot execute payment immediately
Prospect has access to alternative payment method at a known future time (e.g., payday)
claims.mechanism: Separating commitment signature from payment execution removes the binary choice (buy now or not); the contract on file serves as the psychological lock-in, and the 24-hour delay becomes a logistics problem, not an objection.
bounded_by: Does not apply to payment-plan or subscription models where payment must be confirmed before service delivery

claims.text: When a prospect says they don't have the specific card they want to use, ask clarifying questions about the true objection (e.g., "What would make this not a fit for you?") before executing payment alternatives, because sometimes the card objection masks deeper sales resistance about the program itself.
claims.speaker: Dr. Mosey
conditions: Prospect has stated a card-specific payment hesitation
Sales is at or near close stage
claims.mechanism: Diagnostic questioning surfaces whether the objection is a real payment constraint or a signal that the prospect is not genuinely committed to the outcome, which requires re-selling the value proposition rather than just solving logistics.

claims.text: Observing and verbally acknowledging rapport-building details (e.g., 'Oh, you're from Michigan, I have a dog in Michigan') while handling the prospect's ID reinforces trust and softens the perceived invasiveness of requesting payment information.
claims.speaker: Dr. Mosey
claims.mechanism: Personalizing the interaction by referencing external details creates a moment of human connection that reframes the transaction as collaborative rather than transactional.

claims.text: The ID-request-to-card-trade framing should use physical gesture (shaking the ID back toward the wallet or purse) to non-verbally indicate that the prospect needs to expose their payment methods; this reduces the need for explicit verbal asks and creates a natural choreography for the exchange.
claims.speaker: Dr. Mosey
claims.mechanism: Non-verbal cueing (shaking the ID in the direction of the wallet) shifts the psychological burden from "you must do this" to "you must retrieve this," making the prospect a participant rather than a subject.
bounded_by: Requires in-person or video visibility; not applicable to phone-only sales

claims.text: When a prospect says they don't have enough funds, ask what day they get paid and schedule the payment charge for that date, because the deal can close immediately if the prospect confirms commitment; the payment is the confirmation mechanism, not the blocker.
claims.speaker: Dr. Mosey
conditions: Prospect has stated insufficient funds as the objection
Prospect can identify a near-future payday or liquidity event
claims.mechanism: Scheduling payment to align with the prospect's cash inflow timeline removes the financial constraint while the signed contract locks in the psychological commitment.

claims.text: The process prevents the wallet objection from arising in the first place by confirming payment method presence early (via ID request) and framing the close as a permission request ("let me trade you") rather than a demand.
claims.speaker: Dr. Mosey
conditions: Applied throughout the entire close sequence
claims.mechanism: Proactive confirmation that payment methods exist, combined with permissive framing, removes the prospect's ability to claim payment unavailability as a legitimate reason to object.

anchors.value: ~80% will provide payment method without objection using this sequence

examples.text: A prospect pulls out their wallet to show their ID. You notice they have multiple cards visible. You ask them which card they want to use. They say they don't have the specific card they want to use available. You then say, 'Cool, pull your banking app up. What bank do you bank with? Go to statements. Click any month. On the top right you'll see your account number.' You write down the account number and process an ACH transaction instead of a card charge.

A prospect says they don't have enough money to pay today. You ask what day they get paid. They say Friday. You say, 'Great, today is Wednesday. Let's put the charge on Friday when you get paid.' You both set alarms on your phones. The prospect signs the contract. You charge their card on Friday as scheduled.

A prospect hesitates when you ask for payment. Rather than immediately offering alternatives, you say, 'Hey, let me back up a second. I don't want to make you feel uncomfortable. What would make this not a fit for you?' This question surfaces that the real objection is not about payment at all, but about doubts regarding the program's fit for their goals.

practices.text: Set up ACH payment processing with your merchant processor if you don't have it already, because it provides a backup payment path when credit cards are unavailable.
Always request ID before requesting a payment method during closing.
Make a light observation or joke about information on the prospect's ID (e.g., hometown, age) to reinforce rapport while handling their payment method transition.
Use the phrase 'let me trade you for the card you want to use' instead of 'give me your credit card' to frame payment as an exchange rather than a demand.
Physically shake the ID back toward the prospect's wallet or purse to non-verbally indicate they should expose their payment methods rather than asking explicitly.
When a prospect says they don't have the desired card, ask 'Do you have your phone on you?' and walk them through pulling their banking app and statements before defaulting to other alternatives.
If Apple Wallet is not available or the prospect refuses ACH, offer to charge an alternative card and delay the payment 24 hours so they can swap the card at home.
When using the delayed-payment approach, set a mutual phone alarm with the prospect for the time they will be home and available, so you can call them as a reminder to swap the payment method.
